task_description:
# HTML Ingestion Audit: Structural Fidelity and Resource-Fetch Policy (Docling)

## Background
A documentation platform ingests HTML authored by many different tools. Before the HTML pipeline can be trusted, the platform team needs a repeatable **audit tool** that answers two questions about **Docling**'s HTML backend (the `docling` Python package and all of its dependencies are already installed in this environment):

1. **Structural fidelity** — how does the backend turn awkward real-world HTML (ordered lists with hostile `start` attributes, description lists, tables nested inside list items, deeply nested tables carrying images, line breaks, preformatted text, content that precedes the first heading, page footers) into a `DoclingDocument`?
2. **Resource-fetch policy** — when an HTML document references an external or local resource, which locations does the backend resolve, which does it refuse, and under which switches?

The audit must be reproducible and run **fully offline**: the tool must neither perform nor require any network I/O, and it must produce the same report on an air-gapped machine. Every "remote" case in the matrix below is deliberately chosen so that a correct implementation refuses it *before* any connection would be attempted, or is an IP literal that needs no name resolution.

## Requirements
- Convert every `*.html` fixture in a given directory with Docling's HTML backend, using the backend's **default** HTML backend options, and record structural facts about each resulting document: two markdown views (BODY content layer only, and BODY plus FURNITURE), table count, table shapes, table cell texts, and picture count.
- Run a fixed matrix of **resource-location resolutions** through the same resolution logic the HTML backend uses for locations found in a document, and record for each probe whether the location was resolved (and to what) or rejected (and with which error).
- Run a fixed matrix of **image-data loads** through the backend's image-loading logic under specific fetch switches, and record whether the data was loaded (and its size), skipped without data, or blocked (and with which error).
- Run a fixed set of URLs through the backend's remote-URL safety validation and record which are accepted and which are refused.
- Aggregate everything into a single JSON report.
- All facts in the report must be produced by actually exercising Docling in the current environment. The tool is a general audit tool: it will be pointed at different fixture directories and different local resource trees, and it must produce the correct report for whatever it is given.

## Implementation Hints
- Project path: `/home/user/project`
- Everything needed is already installed; do not install packages. The audit tool itself must not perform any network I/O.
- Fixture corpus (already present): `/home/user/project/assets/html/` contains the `*.html` files to audit.
- Local resource tree (already present): `/home/user/project/assets/local/` contains `page.html`, `images/tiny.png` and `images/diagram.svg`.
- Command (rerunnable): `python main.py --html-dir <html_dir> --local-root <local_root> --report <report_path>`
  - It will be invoked from the project directory as:
    `python main.py --html-dir assets/html --local-root assets/local --report output/report.json`
  - All three flags are required. Paths may be relative to the working directory or absolute. Create parent directories of the report if they do not exist. On success, exit with code `0`.
  - If `--html-dir` or `--local-root` does not exist as a directory, write no report, print a diagnostic to stderr, and exit with code `2`.
- Two named base locations are used by the probe matrices below:
  - `LOCAL_BASE` — the **absolute** path of `<local_root>/page.html`.
  - `REMOTE_BASE` — the literal string `https://cdn.example.com/docs/page.html`.

### Report format
The report is a single UTF-8 JSON object with exactly these top-level keys, in this order: `documents`, `resolution_probes`, `fetch_probes`, `url_safety_probes`, `summary`.

**`documents`** — one object per `*.html` file located directly in `<html_dir>` (non-recursive), ordered ascending by file name (Unicode code-point order). Each object has exactly these keys, in this order:
- `name` (string): the file name including its extension.
- `body_lines` (array of strings): take the document's markdown export restricted to the BODY content layer; split it on `"\n"`; right-strip every line; drop every line that is empty after stripping.
- `body_blocks` (array of strings): take the same BODY markdown; split it on `"\n\n"`; strip every element; drop every element that is empty after stripping.
- `full_lines` (array of strings): identical derivation to `body_lines`, but computed from the markdown export that includes **both** the BODY and the FURNITURE content layers.
- `tables` (integer): the number of tables in the converted document.
- `table_shapes` (array): one `[num_rows, num_cols]` integer pair per table, in document order.
- `table_cell_texts` (array): one array per table, in document order, containing the text of each of that table's cells verbatim (in the table's own cell order, no trimming, no substitutions).
- `pictures` (integer): the number of picture items in the converted document.

**`resolution_probes`** — one object per probe below, ordered ascending by `id`. Each probe resolves the given location against the given base location exactly as the HTML backend resolves locations it encounters in a document. Keys, in this order: `id` (string), `outcome` (string, `"resolved"` or `"rejected"`), `resolved` (the returned location string when resolved, otherwise `null`), `error_type` (the raised exception's class name when rejected, otherwise `null`), `error_message` (the raised exception rendered as a string when rejected, otherwise `null`).

| `id` | location | base location |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `abs_posix` | `/etc/passwd` | `LOCAL_BASE` |
| `file_uri` | `file:///etc/passwd` | `LOCAL_BASE` |
| `fragment` | `#section-2` | `LOCAL_BASE` |
| `local_relative` | `images/tiny.png` | `LOCAL_BASE` |
| `protocol_relative` | `//cdn.example.com/img/a.png` | `REMOTE_BASE` |
| `remote_relative` | `img/a.png` | `REMOTE_BASE` |
| `remote_root_relative` | `/img/a.png` | `REMOTE_BASE` |
| `traversal` | `../../../../etc/passwd` | `LOCAL_BASE` |
| `traversal_sneaky` | `images/../../../../etc/passwd` | `LOCAL_BASE` |
| `windows_drive` | `C:\Windows\System32\config\sam` | `LOCAL_BASE` |

**`fetch_probes`** — one object per probe below, ordered ascending by `id`. Each probe hands the given source string, **as-is** (it is not resolved again), to the backend's image-data loading step, with the given base location and the given switches in effect. Any switch not mentioned keeps its default value. Keys, in this order: `id` (string), `outcome` (string: `"loaded"` if image bytes were returned, `"skipped"` if the load completed without returning data and without raising, `"blocked"` if it raised), `num_bytes` (integer length of the returned bytes when loaded, otherwise `null`), `error_type` (the raised exception's class name when blocked, otherwise `null`), `error_message` (the raised exception rendered as a string when blocked, otherwise `null`).

| `id` | source | base location | switches |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `data_uri_ok` | `data:image/png;base64,` followed by the base64 encoding of the exact bytes of `<local_root>/images/tiny.png` | none | maximum accepted base64 image payload: `1024` bytes |
| `data_uri_too_large` | `data:image/png;base64,` followed by the base64 encoding of 2048 NUL bytes (`b"\x00" * 2048`) | none | maximum accepted base64 image payload: `1024` bytes |
| `local_disabled` | the absolute path of `<local_root>/images/tiny.png` | `LOCAL_BASE` | defaults only |
| `local_enabled` | the absolute path of `<local_root>/images/tiny.png` | `LOCAL_BASE` | local resource fetching enabled |
| `local_no_base_path` | `images/tiny.png` | none | local resource fetching enabled |
| `remote_disabled` | `https://cdn.example.com/img/a.png` | none | defaults only |
| `svg_skipped` | the absolute path of `<local_root>/images/diagram.svg` | `LOCAL_BASE` | local resource fetching enabled |

**`url_safety_probes`** — one object per probe below, ordered ascending by `id`. Each probe submits the URL to the backend's remote-URL safety validation. Keys, in this order: `id` (string), `url` (string, exactly as listed), `outcome` (string, `"allowed"` if validation passed, `"rejected"` if it raised), `error_type` (the raised exception's class name when rejected, otherwise `null`), `error_message` (the raised exception rendered as a string when rejected, otherwise `null`).

| `id` | url |
| --- | --- |
| `link_local_metadata` | `http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data` |
| `loopback` | `http://127.0.0.1/image.png` |
| `private_a` | `http://10.0.0.1/image.png` |
| `private_c` | `http://192.168.1.1/image.png` |
| `public_literal` | `https://93.184.216.34/image.png` |

**`summary`** — an object with exactly these integer keys, in this order:
- `num_documents`: the number of entries in `documents`.
- `num_tables`: the sum of `tables` over all entries in `documents`.
- `num_pictures`: the sum of `pictures` over all entries in `documents`.
- `num_rejected_resolutions`: the number of `resolution_probes` entries whose `outcome` is `"rejected"`.
- `num_blocked_fetches`: the number of `fetch_probes` entries whose `outcome` is `"blocked"`.
- `num_rejected_urls`: the number of `url_safety_probes` entries whose `outcome` is `"rejected"`.

### Additional constraints
- Some fixtures intentionally contain unusual or private-use characters and malformed markup. Report the markdown exactly as Docling produces it; do not clean, normalize, re-wrap, or otherwise post-process it beyond the splitting/stripping rules stated above.
- Warnings printed by the conversion are acceptable; they must not change the exit code.
- Running the command twice with the same arguments must produce byte-identical reports.

# Verification Plan ## Setup 1. `cd /home/user/project` 2. Remove stale artifacts so every check exercises a fresh run: `rm -f output/report.json /tmp/audit_probe.json /tmp/audit_alt.json` 3. Run the tool: `python main.py --html-dir assets/html --local-root assets/local --report output/report.json` and confirm exit code `0`. The build-time fixture corpus in `assets/html/` contains exactly these 17 files: `br_paragraph.html`, `br_table.html`, `dl_basic.html`, `dl_multi_dd.html`, `dl_orphan_dd.html`, `dl_strong_dt.html`, `furniture_footer.html`, `nested_table_images.html`, `nested_table_in_dd.html`, `nested_table_in_li.html`, `ol_default.html`, `ol_start_0.html`, `ol_start_2.html`, `ol_start_foo.html`, `ol_start_neg5.html`, `pre_block.html`, `table_rowspan_header.html`. The local resource tree in `assets/local/` contains `page.html`, `images/tiny.png` (a 4x4 PNG, well under 1 KB) and `images/diagram.svg`. ## Verification Steps 1. **Artifacts**: `/home/user/project/main.py` exists; `output/report.json` exists, is non-empty, and parses as a JSON object whose top-level keys are exactly `documents`, `resolution_probes`, `fetch_probes`, `url_safety_probes`, `summary`, in that order. 2. **Document inventory**: `documents` has 17 entries whose `name` values, in order, are exactly the 17 file names listed above (ascending). Every entry has exactly the keys `name`, `body_lines`, `body_blocks`, `full_lines`, `tables`, `table_shapes`, `table_cell_texts`, `pictures`, in that order, with the documented types. 3. **Ordered-list `start` semantics** (`body_lines` of each fixture): - `ol_default.html` → `["1. 1st item", "2. 2nd item"]` - `ol_start_2.html` → `["2. 1st item", "3. 2nd item"]` - `ol_start_0.html` → `["0. 1st item", "1. 2nd item"]` - `ol_start_neg5.html` → `["1. 1st item", "2. 2nd item"]` - `ol_start_foo.html` → `["1. 1st item", "2. 2nd item"]` 4. **Description lists** (`body_lines`): - `dl_basic.html` → `["- **Coffee**", " - Black hot drink", "- **Milk**", " - White cold drink"]` - `dl_multi_dd.html` → `["- **Python**", " - A high-level programming language", " - Known for simplicity"]` - `dl_strong_dt.html` → `["- **HTML**", " - HyperText Markup Language"]` - `dl_orphan_dd.html` → `["- Orphan description 1", "- Orphan description 2"]` 5. **Content-layer separation** (`furniture_footer.html`): - `body_lines` → `["# Main Heading", "Some Content"]` - `full_lines` → `["Initial content with some **bold text**", "# Main Heading", "Some Content", "Some Footer Content"]` 6. **Line-break semantics** (`br_paragraph.html`): - `body_blocks` contains the single block `"This sentence is split across source newlines and must stay together."` (source newlines collapsed to spaces). - `body_blocks` contains the single block `"foo\nbar"` (one `
` is a line break inside one block), and does **not** contain a standalone block equal to `"bar"`. - `body_blocks` contains `"alpha"` and `"beta"` as two separate blocks (two consecutive `
` split the paragraph). - `body_blocks` contains the single block `"Street 1\nCity"`. - `body_blocks` contains the block `"Text with a pre-existing sentinelcharacter."`, and no string anywhere in this document entry contains the private-use character `U+E000`. 7. **Preformatted text** (`pre_block.html`): `body_lines` contains `"Line 1"`, `"Line 2"`, `"Line 3"` as three consecutive entries in that order; `full_lines[0]` is `"# Preformatted"` (the HTML `` is furniture, not body). 8. **Line breaks inside table cells** (`br_table.html`): `tables` is `1`, `table_shapes` is `[[2, 2]]`, and `table_cell_texts[0]` is `["Cell 1\nLine 2", "Plain", "Cell A\n\nCell B", "Plain 2"]`. 9. **Table nested in a list item** (`nested_table_in_li.html`): `tables` is `1`, `table_shapes` is `[[2, 2]]`; `body_lines` contains `"1. First step."`, `"2. Second step:"` and `"3. Third step."` (numbering preserved, the cell's inner `<ul>` is not hoisted into the ordered list); the substring `"Fault type."` occurs exactly once across all of `body_lines` joined with `"\n"` (no duplication of cell text into the list item). 10. **Table nested in a description-list item** (`nested_table_in_dd.html`): `tables` is `1` and `table_shapes` is `[[1, 2]]`. 11. **Nested tables carrying images** (`nested_table_images.html`): the fixture nests 6 tables, each holding exactly one `<img>`; `tables` is `6` and `pictures` is `6` (exactly one picture per `<img>`, no quadratic blow-up). 12. **Spanning header cells** (`table_rowspan_header.html`): `tables` is `1`, `table_shapes` is `[[3, 3]]`, and `table_cell_texts[0]` is `["Region", "Sales", "Q1", "Q2", "North", "10", "20"]`. 13. **Resolution probes**: `resolution_probes` has exactly 10 entries whose `id`s ascend as `abs_posix`, `file_uri`, `fragment`, `local_relative`, `protocol_relative`, `remote_relative`, `remote_root_relative`, `traversal`, `traversal_sneaky`, `windows_drive`; each entry has exactly the keys `id`, `outcome`, `resolved`, `error_type`, `error_message` in that order. - `abs_posix`, `file_uri`, `windows_drive` → `outcome` `"rejected"`, `error_type` `"ValueError"`, `error_message` contains `Absolute paths are not allowed with local base_path`. - `traversal`, `traversal_sneaky` → `outcome` `"rejected"`, `error_type` `"ValueError"`, `error_message` contains `Path traversal blocked`. - `fragment` → `outcome` `"resolved"`, `resolved` `"#section-2"`. - `local_relative` → `outcome` `"resolved"`, `resolved` equal to the absolute path of `/home/user/project/assets/local/images/tiny.png`. - `protocol_relative` → `resolved` `"https://cdn.example.com/img/a.png"`. - `remote_relative` → `resolved` `"https://cdn.example.com/docs/img/a.png"`. - `remote_root_relative` → `resolved` `"https://cdn.example.com/img/a.png"`. - Every rejected entry has `resolved` `null`; every resolved entry has `error_type` and `error_message` `null`. 14. **Fetch probes**: `fetch_probes` has exactly 7 entries whose `id`s ascend as `data_uri_ok`, `data_uri_too_large`, `local_disabled`, `local_enabled`, `local_no_base_path`, `remote_disabled`, `svg_skipped`; each entry has exactly the keys `id`, `outcome`, `num_bytes`, `error_type`, `error_message` in that order. - `data_uri_ok` → `"loaded"`, `num_bytes` equals the byte size of `assets/local/images/tiny.png`. - `data_uri_too_large` → `"blocked"`, `error_type` `"ValueError"`, `error_message` contains `exceeds size limit`. - `local_disabled` → `"blocked"`, `error_type` `"OperationNotAllowed"`, `error_message` contains `Fetching local resources is only allowed when set explicitly`. - `local_enabled` → `"loaded"`, `num_bytes` equals the byte size of `assets/local/images/tiny.png`. - `local_no_base_path` → `"blocked"`, `error_type` `"OperationNotAllowed"`, `error_message` contains `Local file access requires base_path`. - `remote_disabled` → `"blocked"`, `error_type` `"OperationNotAllowed"`, `error_message` contains `Fetching remote resources is only allowed when set explicitly`. - `svg_skipped` → `"skipped"`, `num_bytes` `null`, `error_type` `null`. 15. **URL safety probes**: `url_safety_probes` has exactly 5 entries whose `id`s ascend as `link_local_metadata`, `loopback`, `private_a`, `private_c`, `public_literal`; each entry has exactly the keys `id`, `url`, `outcome`, `error_type`, `error_message` in that order. - `link_local_metadata`, `loopback`, `private_a`, `private_c` → `"rejected"`, `error_type` `"ValueError"`, `error_message` contains `Access to restricted IP address not allowed`. - `public_literal` → `"allowed"`, `error_type` `null`, `error_message` `null`, and its `url` is `https://93.184.216.34/image.png`. 16. **Summary**: `summary` keys are exactly `num_documents`, `num_tables`, `num_pictures`, `num_rejected_resolutions`, `num_blocked_fetches`, `num_rejected_urls` in that order, with the values `17`, `10`, `6`, `5`, `4`, `4` respectively (these also equal the aggregates recomputed from the arrays). 17. **Works on a different corpus (no hard-coding)**: create a temporary directory containing exactly one file `probe.html` with the content `<html><body><ol start="7"><li>alpha</li><li>beta</li></ol></body></html>`, then run `python main.py --html-dir <tmp_html_dir> --local-root assets/local --report /tmp/audit_probe.json`. Expected: exit code `0`; the report's `documents` has exactly one entry, named `probe.html`, whose `body_lines` are `["7. alpha", "8. beta"]`; `summary.num_documents` is `1`. 18. **Works on a different local tree (no hard-coding)**: create a temporary local root containing `page.html`, `images/diagram.svg` and a freshly generated `images/tiny.png` (a different, sub-kilobyte PNG), then run `python main.py --html-dir assets/html --local-root <tmp_local_root> --report /tmp/audit_alt.json`. Expected: exit code `0`; in that report the `local_relative` resolution probe resolves to the absolute path of `<tmp_local_root>/images/tiny.png`, and the `data_uri_ok` and `local_enabled` fetch probes both report `num_bytes` equal to the byte size of that new PNG. 19. **Error handling**: `python main.py --html-dir assets/missing_html --local-root assets/local --report /tmp/audit_missing.json` exits with code `2` and creates no report file; likewise `python main.py --html-dir assets/html --local-root assets/missing_local --report /tmp/audit_missing.json` exits with code `2` and creates no report file. 20. **Determinism**: running the main command twice writes byte-identical reports.
